description: Add `mo label update <key>` to the CLI and a project-scoped label catalog management page to the Web UI. Both consume the existing catalog CRUD API (including PATCH); no server or domain change.

tasks.title: CLI: add `mo label update <key>` with partial-field updates
tasks.spec: specs/cli-interface/spec.md#mo label update modifies user catalog entries
tasks.description: Add an `update` subcommand to the `label` command group in `packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.Label.cs`, registered alongside `list`/`add`/`remove`. It accepts `<key>`, optional `--description`, optional `--supported-values` (comma-separated), the shared `--project`/`--project-id` overrides. It validates the key with `LabelDelta.ValidateKey`, requires at least one field, validates provided fields (non-empty description; non-empty supported-values entries), then sends only the provided fields via the existing `api.PrintPatchAsync` to `PATCH /api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog/{key}`. Server errors (404 unknown key, 400 validation, 409 conflict / system-entry protection) are surfaced clearly with a non-zero exit.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo label update <key> --description "..."` sends PATCH to `/api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog/<key>` carrying only `description`, leaving `supportedValues` unchanged (partial update).
`mo label update <key> --supported-values a,b,c` sends only `supportedValues`, leaving `description` unchanged; supplying both sends both.
An invalid key (e.g. `Module`), an empty `--description`, or an empty `--supported-values` entry is rejected client-side with a clear error, non-zero exit, and no HTTP request sent.
A no-op invocation (neither `--description` nor `--supported-values`) is rejected client-side with a clear error.
An unknown key (API 404) and an attempt to modify a system-origin entry (API 409) are surfaced as clear errors with a non-zero exit; the CLI does not report success.

New tests are added to `packages/cli/tests/Mohist.Cli.Tests/CliLabelCatalogSpecs.cs` covering: description-only update, supported-values-only update, both-fields update, invalid-key pre-validation, empty-description rejection, unknown-key 404 mapping, and system-entry 409 mapping.
`npm test` passes (solution builds with `TreatWarningsAsErrors` and the CLI test suite is green); existing server label-catalog API specs remain green, confirming no API regression.
tasks.output: `packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.Label.cs` gains `BuildUpdate` and registers it; `packages/cli/tests/Mohist.Cli.Tests/CliLabelCatalogSpecs.cs` extended; `npm test` green.
tasks.notes: Reuse `api.PrintPatchAsync` (already in `MohistCliApi.cs`) — do not add a new HTTP helper. Omit absent fields from the PATCH body rather than sending null, so 'keep current' stays distinct from 'clear'.

tasks.title: Web UI: project-scoped label catalog management Settings tab
tasks.spec: specs/web-ui/spec.md#Web UI provides a project-scoped label catalog management page
tasks.description: Add a new `entities/label-catalog` data slice (`model/types.ts`, `api/client.ts`, `api/queries.ts`) over the existing catalog endpoints (`GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog`) using the shared `request()` + `projectApiPath()` helpers, plus a `pages/settings/ui/LabelCatalogSection.tsx` component registered as a new tab in `SettingsPage.tsx` (`VALID_SECTIONS`, `SECTION_META`, and the `SectionContent` switch). The section lists every entry (key/description/supportedValues/origin), lets users add user-origin definitions, edit an entry's description and supportedValues (key immutable), and delete user entries (delete hidden/disabled for origin=system). Client-side validation enforces `key =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`, non-empty description, and non-empty supported values; API errors are surfaced in-page.
acceptanceCriteria: The Settings page exposes a new 'Label catalog' tab reachable at `/settings/<section>`, registered in `VALID_SECTIONS`, `SECTION_META`, and the `SectionContent` switch in `packages/web/src/pages/settings/ui/SettingsPage.tsx`.
The tab lists every catalog entry showing `key`, `description`, `supportedValues` (when present), and `origin` (system/user).
An add form creates user-origin entries (`key`, `description`, optional `supportedValues`) via `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog`; the new entry appears with `origin: user`.
Editing an entry updates `description` and/or `supportedValues` via `PATCH /api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog/<key>`; the `key` field is not editable in the form.
Deleting a user-origin entry sends `DELETE /api/projects/{projectRef}/labels/catalog/<key>` and removes it from the list.
For `origin: system` rows, both the edit and delete actions are hidden or disabled and no modifying or destructive request is sent (system definitions are read-only).
An invalid key (uppercase, leading dash, etc.) or whitespace-only description is rejected before any request with a clear in-page validation error.
API failures (400 / 404 / 409) are surfaced in-page with the server-provided message and the list is not left in an inconsistent state (TanStack Query cache invalidated/rolled back appropriately).
Adding, editing, or removing a catalog entry does not modify any issue's labels (the catalog stays advisory).

Component tests in `packages/web/src/pages/settings/ui/` (and the slice's `queries.test.ts` where applicable) cover: list render, add, edit (key immutable), delete, system-entry read-only protection (edit + delete), and client-side validation rejection.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` both pass.
tasks.output: New `entities/label-catalog/` slice; new `pages/settings/ui/LabelCatalogSection.tsx`; `SettingsPage.tsx` registration; component + slice tests; web typecheck and test runs green.
tasks.notes: Placement follows RepositoriesSection as the closest project-scoped CRUD analog. supportedValues editor is a comma/newline-separated text input parsed to a string[] (a chip/tag editor is explicitly deferred). Omit absent fields on PATCH rather than sending null. Do NOT touch the issue-level LabelEditor.
